title: Copilot Studio: credit costs per agent and by lifecycle stage in the Monitor tab
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, billing qualifications and existing spending controls are supported by Microsoft's documentation, including the updated capacity page. The allocation API exists despite the automatic warning; minor corrections concern its presentation and a reporting checklist step without a controls-table row.

claims.claim: The planned display includes per-agent costs and an estimated lifecycle breakdown.
claims.quote: at both a per-agent level and an estimated breakdown of those costs across the agents lifecylce

claims.claim: The roadmap names authoring, testing, evaluations and production usage as example activities.
claims.quote: activities such as authoring, testing, evaluations, and production usage

claims.claim: Learn does not identify its existing Monitor credit displays as roadmap item 571196.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com Monitor cost 571196 Copilot'; opened agents-experience/analytics-overview, billing-credit-understand-display, authoring-review-activity and analytics-consumption; none identifies item 571196.

claims.claim: For the Microsoft Copilot harness, Monitor includes a Total estimated credits used metric.
claims.quote: **Total estimated credits used**: The credits the agent consumed during the selected period.

claims.claim: When available, that breakdown estimates consumption across production usage, preview testing, evaluations and other supported surfaces.
claims.quote: When a breakdown is available, it shows an estimated split of consumption by experience, including production usage, preview testing, evaluations, and other supported surfaces.

claims.claim: For standard-harness agents billed on Copilot Credits consumption, Monitor's Overview panel shows total billed Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: On the **Monitor** page for your agent, the **Overview** panel shows your agent's total billed Copilot Credits for the selected time period.

claims.claim: The standard-harness billing view includes a Billing trend chart.
claims.quote: The **Billing trend** chart shows the changes in your agent's billed Copilot Credits over the selected time period.

claims.claim: The standard-harness Cost distribution chart shows activity types that count towards Copilot Credits consumption.
claims.quote: The **Cost distribution** chart shows which kinds of activity count towards Copilot Credits usage.

claims.claim: The documented Monitor breakdown's list does not explicitly name authoring as a category.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio Monitor lifecycle breakdown separate licensing credit rate'; opened agents-experience/analytics-overview and billing-credit-understand-display. The breakdown names production usage, preview testing, evaluations and other supported surfaces, not authoring.

claims.claim: Microsoft's governance article recommends classifying environments as exploration, test and production.
claims.quote: **Classify**: Label each environment as exploration and prototyping, test and validation, or funded production.

claims.claim: The existing agent-limit management page is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents.
claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select **Licensing**.
In the **Licensing** pane, under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
On the **Summary** tab, select **Manage Agents**.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation for the existing Power Platform per-agent monthly limit was found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio monthly credit limit agent Power Platform API Dataverse bot table Set limit'; 'Copilot Studio monthly credit limits PowerShell pac admin automation'. Read governance, capacity, allocation tutorial; searched bot table, Power Apps PowerShell and pac admin references.

claims.claim: Agent-limit management supports notifications to environment and tenant administrators as usage approaches the monthly limit.
claims.quote: **Notifications**: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.claim: The existing allocation management pane is reached through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote:
In the **Licensing** pane, under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
Select the **Summary** tab.
Under the **Copilot Studio** heading, select **Manage Copilot Credits** or **Manage sessions**.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 accepts the printed environment scope, MCSMessages allocation quantity and enforcementRules body.
claims.quote:
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" `
    -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody
claims.fix: Replace the call in the structured row and rendered table with 'PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01'. Replace the note's opening '<rule> is ...' sentence with 'The request body sets scope.environmentId and allocatedEntitlements, with entitlementId MCSMessages, allocation.quantity, and enforcementRules containing ruleType TenantPool and enabled true or false.' Retain the environment-group override qualification.

claims.claim: The TenantPool enforcement rule's enabled value controls whether an environment draws from unallocated tenant capacity.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted; when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule governing tenant-capacity draw prevents an individual environment override.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.

claims.claim: UI, API and administration SDK attempts to override that rule are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Managing allocations requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role permitted to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop agent flows called by that agent.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately

claims.claim: Agent limits do not cap aggregate environment consumption.
claims.quote: Agent limits don't cap aggregate environment consumption.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center has no tenant-wide default agent limit, so an organisation's standard limit must be applied to individual agents.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center doesn't provide a tenant-wide default agent limit. If your organization defines a standard limit for new agents, use a recurring or automated process to apply it to individual agents.

claims.claim: Changing and republishing the environment-group rule is a documented way to change policy-governed tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group

claims.claim: Removing an environment from its group is a documented way to restore independent management of tenant-capacity draw.
claims.quote: remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently. After removal, the environment retains the value last applied by the group, but the setting becomes editable.

claims.claim: Microsoft's governance article points to Power Platform API entitlement insight operations for programmatic consumption data.
claims.quote: At scale or when using automation, use the entitlement insight operations in the Power Platform API to retrieve consumption data programmatically.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio environment and agent spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center are opt-in.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio environment and agent policies are opt-in

claims.claim: Existing Power Platform controls continue applying until a Microsoft 365 spending policy covers the relevant scope.
claims.quote: existing Power Platform admin center controls continue to apply until a Microsoft 365 spending policy covers that scope

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe an administrative control specific to the roadmap's Monitor cost display.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio Monitor cost visibility rollout default enable disable lifecycle breakdown'; 'Copilot Studio Monitor enable cost permissions'. Opened both agents-experience Monitor pages, sharing, capacity and cost-management documentation; no switch specific to this display.

claims.claim: The checklist directs readers to compare consumption reports, but the controls table has no reporting row.
claims.quote: Compare a maker's Monitor figure with the Power Platform admin center consumption report for the same agent and period; controls rows cover monthly agent limits and environment credit allocation only.
claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet beginning 'Compare a maker's Monitor figure with the Power Platform admin center consumption report'; it names a reporting control absent from the table. The existing explanation of billed versus non-billed figures can remain.
